title: optimistic-fastpath-prefetch-kv-probe-gating
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: Production workloads occasionally hit a pessimistic fallback that serializes small batches and disables KV prefix caching when kernel compatibility heuristics are uncertain. This PR implements an optimistic fast-path that probes the KV cache and prefetches likely KV slots while maintaining a conservative safety fallback. Motivation: reduce p99 latency regressions introduced by broad safe-mode gating, without sacrificing correctness under model/kernel incompatibilities. Summary of changes: 1) optimistic_fastpath: new scheduler path that attempts a non-blocking KV-probe on request arrival, dispatching to fast kernels when probe + kernel predicate both pass; 2) kv_probe_prefetch: lightweight probe that checks prefix presence with an adjustable probe budget and issues asynchronous prefetches for adjacent KV shards; 3) kernel_compat_check: deferred compatibility check that runs in parallel with batching time window and only forces fallback if incompatibility is confirmed; 4) batching_adapter: small change to continuous batching to allow short wait windows (configurable) for the optimistic path; 5) metrics and tracing: counters for probe_hits/probe_misses, prefetch_success, fastpath_take_rate, and histograms for fastpath vs fallback latencies; 6) tests and benchmarks: microbench for workload with 50% cache locality and end-to-end integration tests that validate deterministic correctness when probe budget is exhausted. Design notes: the fastpath is intentionally optimistic - it privileges latency by attempting prefetches and dispatching to quantized kernels immediately when the probe returns a confident hit. A light-weight token-bucket probe_budget prevents probe storms on heavy-tail request spikes. If the probe misses or kernel_compat_check returns unknown / fails, the request is routed to the safe fallback which runs full verification and uses the conservative kernel codepath. The deferred kernel check ensures that a fastpath dispatch can be rolled back early in the request pipeline if a critical mismatch is detected, avoiding silent correctness violations. CI and validation: initial CI runs showed intermittent flakiness in the integration test under heavy parallelism (race in probe cache initialization) which was fixed by introducing a one-time init with compare-and-swap and expanding the test's warmup. Performance: on the benchmark harness this change reduced p50 by ~6-8% and p99 by ~18-25% for a mixed-locality chat workload (50% prefix hits, sequence length 256) with negligible throughput regression. Rollout and risk controls: feature gated under runtime.config.optimistic_fastpath_enabled (off by default); telemetry includes a safety-assertion counter that triggers automatic rollback if the fallback_count / total_requests ratio exceeds a configurable threshold for a 5-minute window. Related work: complements ENG-1604 adaptive kernel selector and addresses regressions observed after the safe-mode-wide toggle applied in SUP-4217 incident. Implementation notes: careful attention paid to memory ordering in the prefetch path and to avoid long-lived locks in the scheduler hot path. See changed_files for details. This description is intentionally compact; see commits, changed_files and review_comments fields for more context.

ci_summary: Initial CI: integration test flake (fixed) -> subsequent runs: build + unit + integration + perf all passed; benchmark CI shows expected p99 improvements; pre-merge lint warnings fixed in second commit
release_notes: Introduce an opt-in optimistic fastpath that probes and prefetches KV prefixes to accelerate high-locality workloads. Off by default. Reduces p99 latency in mixed-locality scenarios while providing a conservative fallback when kernel compatibility is uncertain. Includes new telemetry and rollout controls.
notes_for_rollback: Feature is behind a runtime flag and telemetry guard rails. To rollback: set runtime.config.optimistic_fastpath_enabled=false and monitor fastpath.* metrics; if safety_assertions spike, revert by disabling flag and triggering config rollout.
manual_test_steps: 1) Start runtime with optimistic_fastpath_enabled=true and probe_budget=4

notes: This PR was coordinated with platform and SRE to ensure rollout controls; telemetry dashboards included in the commit. We intentionally kept the fastpath conservative by default to reduce blast radius for customers.
